The city-wide 'continental rice at most once a week' cap is meant for a mixed counter that sees continental once, and contradicts a station whose whole purpose is continental — it made this counter INFEASIBLE on every odd week. Scoped off here only; Amadeus's South and North counters still obey it.

The weekday pattern is not expressible as a theme, so it uses components_by_weekday; an empty list means 'compose nothing that day'. The Tue/Thu blanks come from infenion_nonveg_mon_wed_fri below. Monday excludes is_egg_dish because two egg dishes (egg_drumstick_curry, egg_kurma) are wrongly flagged is_south_chicken_gravy in the ontology.

Non Veg Lunch._comment: This counter is themed biryani on all five days, so the theme filter leaves nonveg biryani as the only option every day. The city rule 'nonveg_biryani_once_per_week' is a weekly-variety cap written for a mixed counter and contradicts that by construction. Confirmed with the client that biryani daily is intended, so the cap is dropped here — scoped to this counter, so L&T's South and North Lunch counters keep it if they ever gain a nonveg_main slot. This is also the 5-dish station: with nonveg_main set to 5, 'nonveg_main_five_dish' composes biryani + gravy + dry + kebab + egg each day.

rules._comment: The printed menu serves the same EGG CURRY on all five days, alongside the same CHICKEN KABAB - both are fixtures on this station, not variety slots. The kebab is fixed by accident (one eligible tandoor item); the egg needs saying, because 21 egg dishes are eligible and the solver would otherwise serve five different ones. This rule also declares its items repeatable so unique_items does not forbid the repetition.
rules.name: lt_egg_same_every_day

Non Veg Lunch._comment: Themed biryani on two weekdays (Wed + Fri) against the city cap of one biryani day per week. Before the composition rule applied to 3-slot counters this contradiction was hidden — the solver satisfied the cap by putting its one biryani day on a mix day and leaving both biryani days without one. Client confirmed two biryani days are intended, so the weekly cap is dropped for this counter only.

constant_items._comment: Wednesday only, ONE non-veg main, alternating weekly: Hyd Mutton Biryani one week and Fish Tikka Masala the next, in the same slot (nonveg_main__1). Neither is in the Bangalore ontology (chicken + egg only), so it stamps verbatim. The list value = alternate across ISO weeks (even week -> first, odd -> second); see _resolve_client_constant / CLAUDE.md note 9. The other two non-veg mains and every non-Wednesday day are solved normally.

ToastTab CHN._comment: Chennai. Derived from a 7-day SERVICE HISTORY (Wed 01 Jul – Thu 09 Jul 2026, weekdays only), not a written rulebook — see docs/chennai_client_logic.md for the grid and how each rule was read off it. THE ONE ASSUMPTION: the sample spans two part-weeks whose weekday→theme mapping conflicts (Wed is south on 01 Jul but biryani on 08 Jul; Thu is north on 02 Jul but south on 09 Jul), so the theme map is inferred from the later, more complete run 06–09 Jul — Mon/Thu/Fri south, Tue north, Wed biryani. That fits 5 of the 7 observed days and reproduces the sample's 4 south : 2 north : 1 biryani ratio scaled to a 5-day week. The weekday lists below FOLLOW from that map: if the real theme map differs, these lists must move with it, because what the sample actually determines is the THEME each slot belongs to, not the weekday.

rules._comment: White rice on the SOUTH days only. The sample is 7/7 on this: white rice appears on every south day and on no north or biryani day, where a flavoured rice takes its place — one rice per day, never two (the same structure Amadeus Pune has).
rules.name: toast_tab_chn_white_rice_south_days

rules._comment: Flavoured rice on the NORTH and BIRYANI days only — peas pulao (north), ghee bisibelebath (north), veg biryani (biryani) in the sample. Complement of the white-rice list, so exactly one rice fills every day.
rules.name: toast_tab_chn_flavour_rice_north_biryani_days

rules._comment: Rasam on the SOUTH days only — the 'RASAM / CURD' cell, which the source workbook auto-split into two servings. It appears on all four south days and none of the others: with no plain rice to eat it with, a north or biryani day serves curd rice instead.
rules.name: toast_tab_chn_rasam_south_days

rules._comment: The curd half of 'RASAM / CURD', same four south days. The biryani day's RAITHA is a curd_side too, which is why `wed` is included here but not in the rasam list — a biryani gets a raita, not a rasam.
rules.name: toast_tab_chn_curd_side_south_and_biryani_days

rules._comment: Curd rice on the NORTH and BIRYANI days — the sour/yogurt component when there is no white rice + rasam. 3/3 in the sample.
rules.name: toast_tab_chn_curd_rice_north_biryani_days

rules._comment: Overrides the city rule of the same name (merged by name, so this REPLACES chennai.json's max of 1). Chennai's cap of one maida bread a week is simply wrong for this client: the sample serves a maida bread on 4 of 7 days (aloo paratha, butter kulcha, kothu parotta, paratha) and only 3 of the 5 non-maida wheat breads in the whole 29-dish pool are chapati variants. Client-confirmed at 2 a week, replacing the 3 I had read off the sample (which serves a maida bread on 4 of 7 days). Feasible because only the maida DAYS are capped: the 5 non-maida wheat flatbreads include the chapati family, which plain_chapati_may_repeat exempts from uniqueness, so the remaining 3 days draw from a 5-dish pool. Without this the pre-flight gate correctly answered 422: the wheat-flatbread composition below forces a maida bread on days the cap forbids.
rules.name: maida_bread_weekly

rules._comment: The bread is always a wheat or maida flat bread, never the dosai/idly family. Every one of the seven sampled breads is chapati, paratha, kulcha or kothu parotta; Chennai's 29-dish bread pool also holds 9 rice-breads (dosai, idly, appam) and the solver picked 'podi idly' as a bread row until this was added. A one-slot composition component with count 1 IS 'this slot must be a matching dish' (note 20) — `fixed_daily_item` would be the wrong tool, it only makes the choice consistent.
rules.name: toast_tab_chn_bread_is_a_wheat_flatbread

Amadeus Pune._comment: Amadeus Pune — from the client's sample week (docs/pune_client_logic.md). Seven service days: Mon-Fri full, Saturday drops the veg dry, Sunday is flavoured rice (a veg biryani) with raita, papad, buttermilk and a sweet and nothing else. The raita comes from the Curd / Raita category the client configured, restricted to Sunday — the day the biryani wants it.

So white rice runs on exactly the days the flavoured-rice slot does NOT (Mon, Wed, Thu, Fri, Sat) — it used to include Tue, which put Tawa Pulao AND steamed rice on the same day. Kept as a weekday list rather than a rule keyed off the flavoured-rice slot because both slots are day-restricted to fixed weekdays; if 'flavour rice on Tue and sun' ever changes, this list changes with it.

rules._comment: 'chapati daily in indain bread' — a per-day MANDATE, not merely permission to repeat. On a one-slot family a slot_composition component with count 1 means 'this slot must be a matching dish', so bread is chapati on every day it is served. fixed_daily_item was the wrong tool: it only makes the matching dish CONSISTENT across days and leaves the solver free to serve phulka instead, which it did. The city ruleset's plain_chapati_may_repeat supplies the unique_items / cooldown exemption the repetition needs.

rules._comment: Buttermilk runs every day, so it must be exempt from unique_items and from the 20-day cooldown. The city ruleset declares no welcome-drink staple (R59 was ambiguous until this client answered it), so the declaration is scoped here.

DXC._comment: Bangalore launch site (created via the launch view). Uses the Bangalore regional ruleset + these DXC logics; the two counters (Veg Lunch, Non Veg Lunch) both carry bread/rice/curd_side so these are client-level. The 'common categories are identical across both counters' requirement is handled by shared_categories below: the planner solves the primary counter and pins its dish for each shared slot into the other counter per day (see docs/client_logics.md gap 1).
DXC._disable_comment: Two Bangalore base rules contradict DXC's stated logic and must be dropped, not overridden. (1) mixedveg_pulao_biryani_weekly caps combined biryani+pulao at 1 day/week (variety) — DXC wants biryani 3x AND pulao 1x, so the cap is force-violated. (2) curd_raita_logic forces raita on every biryani/pulao day and plain curd otherwise; DXC serves 4 flavoured-rice days but wants raita Mon/Tue/Thu/Fri and plain curd Wed on a single curd_side slot, so the convention collides with the client's explicit weekday schedule (Wed is usually a biryani/pulao day). The theme filter is NOT exempted for rice: biryani is already placeable on north/mix days here (verified), so no override is needed.
DXC._shared_categories_comment: Cross-counter sync: these categories serve the SAME dish on both counters each day (DXC's 'common categories are identical across counters'). The planner solves the primary counter (index 0), then pins its choice for each of these base slots into every other counter on the matching day (client-orchestrated, via /plan's shared_items). white_rice is included because plain steamed rice should also match; add/remove a base slot here to change the shared set.

rules._comment: Flavoured rice: biryani at least 3 days a week, even on non-biryani days (the client's 'flavour rice biryani 3x even if not biryani day').

rules._comment: Indian bread is plain chapati every day. A slot_composition component (not fixed_daily_item, which only makes the dish CONSISTENT and lets the solver serve a non-matching bread — see CLAUDE.md note 20) mandates a plain_chapatti/phulka item (plain_chapatti or plain_phulka) in the single bread cell each day.

rules._comment: Plain chapati is a staple: only 2 such items exist, so daily service must repeat them. Exempt from unique_items and the 20-day cooldown, else week 2 has both in history and the mandate above goes INFEASIBLE (same R36/Pune pattern).
rules.name: dxc_plain_chapati_repeatable

rules._comment: Curd side: raita Mon/Tue/Thu/Fri, plain curd on Wednesday. Per-weekday composition on the single curd_side slot; the base curd_raita_logic is disabled above so it does not fight this schedule.
